stories.title: Mayor Mamdani and Chancellor Samuels Put Students First with Nation’s Broadest Generative AI Moratorium in Schools
stories.simple_summary: New York City's leaders have stopped schools from using AI tools in a big way. This is one of the broadest restrictions on AI in schools anywhere in the country.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have children or grandchildren in NYC schools, their teachers won't be using AI to help grade papers or teach lessons for now.

stories.title: Schools respond to disturbing ‘Cat in the Hat’ trend from A.I.-generated photos
stories.simple_summary: Schools are dealing with a problem where AI is creating fake, disturbing photos of characters like the Cat in the Hat. Students are sharing these online.
stories.why_it_matters: School leaders need to know what images their students are exposed to and creating — this is a safety issue similar to other concerning content kids encounter online.

stories.title: The Builders Stage brings practical strategies for scaling startups to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: A technology conference is hosting a stage where startup founders and business leaders talk about how to grow their companies. This is mostly relevant to investors and people in the tech industry.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech entrepreneurs — nothing you need to act on unless you're starting a high-tech company.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks paid $500M for Thrive-backed Console, sources say
stories.simple_summary: A big computer security company bought another AI company for $500 million. This is a business deal between large technology companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech industry watchers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s new Real World AI Stage features Nvidia, robots, and extinct animals
stories.simple_summary: A tech conference will have a stage showing how AI works in the real world, with demonstrations involving robots and other physical examples. This is mainly industry-focused.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech professionals and investors interested in where AI is heading — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: OpenAI’s new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI made a new AI model that thinks in a different way than before. Some safety experts worry this new approach might be harder to control.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to AI researchers and safety experts — nothing you need to act on right now, but it's worth knowing that experts have concerns about new AI methods.

stories.title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
stories.simple_summary: Google released a new, faster version of its Gemini AI tool. It can think through harder problems by taking more steps, similar to how you'd solve a complex math problem slowly instead of guessing.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's AI tools for business, the new version works better at complex tasks but may cost slightly more over time — though the starting price is the same.

stories.title: New York City Bans A.I. in Elementary and Middle Schools
stories.simple_summary: New York City is banning AI tools from elementary and middle schools. Teachers won't be allowed to use AI to help with instruction or grading in younger grades.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have young children in NYC schools, their education won't include AI tools the schools control — this is a safety decision about young students.

stories.title: JD Vance talks end times, Antichrist and AI on faith podcast
stories.simple_summary: A political figure discussed AI along with religious topics on a podcast. This is mainly about personal opinions rather than news about AI itself.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters if you're interested in political figures' views — nothing specific about AI you need to act on.

stories.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's Alexa AI helper can now tell you if an email supposedly from Amazon is actually real or a fake scam. You can ask it to check messages for you.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Amazon and get emails or texts claiming to be from the company, you can now ask Alexa to verify if they're real — this helps protect you from scams.

stories.title: Pangram’s Max Spero on why AI detection is harder than ‘Real or Fake’
stories.simple_summary: A company called Pangram is trying to build tools that can tell if text and images were made by AI or are real. They say this is harder than it seems because AI is getting very good at faking things.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a business that relies on reviews or applications from customers, you should know that fake AI-created content is sneaking into these — it's becoming harder to spot what's genuine.

stories.title: We’re ‘dangerously close’ to dead internet theory, says Pangram’s CEO
stories.simple_summary: A CEO warns that the internet is filling up with so much fake AI content that it's becoming hard to know what's real. He calls this close to the "dead internet theory" — the idea that the internet will become mostly fake.
stories.why_it_matters: As you read things online — reviews, news, photos — be more careful about what's real, because AI-made fakes are spreading and getting harder to spot. Trust your gut and check sources you know are reliable.
